brief:
Australia's Royal Commission into Antisemitism has convened hearings over recent months in which Zionist witnesses have denied genocide allegations and characterized Palestinian solidarity activism as hate speech, according to Mondoweiss. The inquiry's proceedings are establishing legal and rhetorical foundations that could criminalize pro-Palestine protest, political speech, and academic scholarship on Palestinian issues for years to come.

The commission's approach has allowed witnesses to reframe Palestine solidarity campaigns as antisemitic conduct rather than legitimate political expression. Legal experts and Palestinian advocates have warned that the inquiry's methodology risks conflating criticism of Israeli government policy with antisemitism, potentially chilling free speech protections and creating precedent for suppressing dissent on Middle East policy across Australian institutions and civil society.
dek: Australia's Royal Commission into Antisemitism has spent months letting Zionist witnesses deny genocide and recast Palestine solidarity as hate, laying the groundwork to criminalize protest, speech, and scholarship on Palestine for years to come.
title: Australian inquiry frames Palestine activism as antisemitism threat
